rr.cite: Baumert M et al. Mean nocturnal respiratory rate predicts cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older men and women. Eur Respir J 2019;54:1802175
rr.finding: Mean nocturnal breathing rate ≥ 16/min (from overnight polysomnography) independently predicted all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older adults: HR 1.18 (95 % CI 1.04–1.32) in 2,686 men, 1.50 (1.02–2.20) in 406 women.

wheeze.cite: Carpenter L, Beral V, Strachan D et al. Respiratory symptoms as predictors of 27 year mortality in a representative sample of British adults. BMJ 1989;299:357–61
wheeze.finding: Wheeze most days or nights (questionnaire, not auscultation) predicted death from chronic bronchitis in men: mortality ratio 10.5 (95 % CI 4.4–24.6); most respiratory symptoms carried 20–50 % higher all-cause death rates, adjusted for age, sex and smoking.
